_doc: R10 SUPPRESSION SWEEP register (DIRECTOR_RULING_FAILURE_BIAS_LAWS 2026-07-27). Every gate/throttle/suppression/fold introduced in the trailing 14 days (git --since=2026-07-13 over background/**), classified by FAILURE DIRECTION (noisy|silent) and assigned a remediation (law_a time-bound+re-arm | law_c independent-counterpart | law_b lane-isolation | none). STANDING CONSEQUENCE (director): no suppression lands without a non-empty `what_still_pages` -- the independent check that fires if the underlying condition is real. Enforced by background/suppression_register.py::validate_suppression_register (R15 both-ways in tests/background/test_suppression_register.py). Human table: docs/observability/suppression_audit_2026-07-27.md.

entries.mechanism: Pending-batch mint gate (rest-with-proof over an all-blocked in_progress batch)
entries.purpose: Stop RUNG-7 planner mint-spam when the pending in_progress batch is all-blocked.

entries.rearm_trigger: 2h rest-proof age cap (supervisor.py:2538) voids the batch-rest and forces planner re-examination; deadman OPEN-MINT >2h + 6h HARD_REST_CAP are un-suppressible.

entries.mechanism: Self-verifying push throttle (only mark the publish throttle satisfied on a VERIFIED origin advance)
entries.purpose: Prevent a bare `git push` rc=0 that did not advance origin from satisfying the publish throttle.
entries.named_failure: none (compliant example -- a throttle that fails TOWARD action)
entries.what_still_pages: the throttle releases (re-pushes) unless ls-remote confirms origin==HEAD -- it fails toward re-attempt, never toward a silent 'pushed' claim. Model example of a noise-biased throttle. COMMITTED_PUSH_THROTTLED (2026-08-13) is the SAME mechanism's outcome label on the deferred-push branch, and it sits in RETRYABLE_PUBLISH_OUTCOMES deliberately: the content IS committed locally, so re-running that identical cycle would correctly find nothing to commit, and the next due cycle pushes it. What still pages if that reasoning is wrong: deadmans_switch._check_content_publishing reads publish_freshness off disk INDEPENDENTLY of this pipeline and pages [PUBLISHING DOWN] once the figures have not reached origin for STALE_AFTER_SECONDS -- so a throttle that stopped releasing surfaces as a publishing outage, not as silence.

entries.mechanism: Publish-gate surgical scope partition (@pytest.mark.operational -- scope blocking tests to the publish surface)
entries.purpose: Stop unrelated test failures from wedging the publish pipeline overnight (R10 close the overnight-wedge class).
entries.named_failure: none directly, but narrowing what blocks publish is silence-shaped
entries.what_still_pages: H23 operational-layer INDEPENDENT green signal (2ddf71272) + reconcile-before-test (abeb41555); a content regression outside the partition still reds the full suite and the next digest. Has a Law-C independent counterpart already.
entries.rearm_trigger: H23 operational-layer INDEPENDENT green signal (2ddf71272) + reconcile-before-test (abeb41555); a content regression OUTSIDE the partition still reds the full suite.

entries.mechanism: External-blocked atom exclusion (the draw excludes atoms carrying blocked_on)
entries.purpose: Stop the loop thrashing on an atom that is genuinely blocked on an external/director act.
entries.named_failure: class-adjacent to failure #2 (a block removing work from the feasible set)
entries.what_still_pages: sibling lanes (site / discovery / forward-discovery / HARDEN) remain drawable, so excluding one blocked atom does not zero the tick; deadman OPEN-MINT escalates any blocked atom left un-worked. LAW B mint hardens per-cluster isolation so an exclusion can never leak across lanes.
entries.rearm_trigger: sibling lanes (site / discovery / forward-discovery / HARDEN) remain drawable, so excluding one blocked atom never zeros the tick; deadman OPEN-MINT escalation fires on the excluded atom if it stays open >2h.

entries.mechanism: BUILD-IN-PROGRESS guard (don't re-offer an atom a live fork already owns)
entries.purpose: Stop the self-drawing loop re-offering an atom a live focused fork is already building.
entries.what_still_pages: fail-open on a stale/missing/malformed marker -> re-offers the atom (biases to work, not silence); deadman fires if the loop rests. R15-proven fail-open.

entries.mechanism: Frame-saturation draw guard (idle DISCOVER/FRAME stops re-handing FRAME-saturated BUILD-gated atoms)
entries.purpose: End the stale-draw treadmill where an idle tick re-hands an atom whose FRAME work is already saturated.
entries.what_still_pages: self-staleness re-exec guard (af8863f47) re-evaluates from disk on the next tick; other draw rungs are unaffected; deadman fires on rest. Independent counterpart already present.
entries.rearm_trigger: the self-staleness re-exec guard (af8863f47) re-evaluates from disk on the next tick; other draw rungs are unaffected; deadman fires on rest -- an independent counterpart, not a self-declaration.

entries.mechanism: Publish-gate wedge-alert cooldown (at most one wedge NTFY per hour while the gate stays wedged, process_run_complete.py)
entries.commit: predates the 14-day sweep window; surfaced + registered by the registration-hole lint (DIRECTOR_RULING_SWEEP_VERDICT 2026-07-27 s1)
entries.purpose: Rate-limit the repeated 'publish gate wedged' NTFY to one per hour so a persistent wedge does not spam the director; the block itself is never rate-limited.
entries.named_failure: none directly -- rate-limiting a repeat alert is silence-shaped, so it is held to the LAW A re-arm requirement
entries.what_still_pages: the publish gate stays BLOCKED (publish_gate_surgical_scope) while wedged -- publishing does not resume silently; the deadman commit-cadence tier fires INDEPENDENTLY of this throttle. The cooldown only rate-limits the DUPLICATE wedge NTFY and re-arms after PUBLISH_GATE_COOLDOWN_SECONDS (1h).
entries.rearm_trigger: cooldown re-arms after PUBLISH_GATE_COOLDOWN_SECONDS (3600s); the wedge block itself is un-throttled and the deadman commit-cadence tier is an independent counterpart.

entries.mechanism: Inbound-NTFY flood-guard alert cooldown (at most one [FLOOD GUARD] NTFY per window while a flood persists, ntfy_responder.py)
entries.commit: predates the 14-day sweep window; surfaced + registered by the registration-hole lint (DIRECTOR_RULING_SWEEP_VERDICT 2026-07-27 s1)
entries.purpose: Rate-limit the [FLOOD GUARD] NTFY while an inbound-NTFY flood persists so the flood alert itself does not become the flood; message quarantine is never rate-limited.
entries.named_failure: none directly -- rate-limiting a repeat alert is silence-shaped, so it is held to the LAW A re-arm requirement
entries.what_still_pages: every flooded message is STILL quarantined to docs/staging/quarantine/ regardless of the alert throttle (the underlying condition is preserved on disk, not silenced); the cooldown only rate-limits the repeat [FLOOD GUARD] NTFY and re-arms after FLOOD_ALERT_COOLDOWN_SECONDS (3600s).
entries.rearm_trigger: cooldown re-arms after FLOOD_ALERT_COOLDOWN_SECONDS (3600s); message quarantine to docs/staging/quarantine/ is un-throttled and independent of the alert cooldown.

law_a_gate: LAW A landed 2026-07-27: every `silent`-biased entry now declares its RE-ARM -- a numeric `max_age_seconds` (time-bound / Law A) and/or a `rearm_trigger` (independent counterpart / Law C). background/suppression_register.py::validate_suppression_register FAILS if a silent suppression declares neither (it could then indefinitely silence a check -- the defect LAW A forbids), or if a `law_a` token lacks the time-bound / a `law_c` token lacks the trigger. R15 both-ways in tests/background/test_suppression_register.py.
